title: Why are clouds white but storm clouds grey?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do rain clouds look dark?
Why do clouds turn pink at sunset?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Same droplets; grey means too thick for light

explain.say: Clouds are made of water droplets much larger than air molecules. Big droplets scatter all colours of light about equally, not just blue, so the scattered light looks white.

draw.text: Why are clouds white but storm clouds grey?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same droplets; grey means too thick for light

explain.say: A thin or small cloud lets sunlight pass through and scatters it towards you from every side, so it glows bright white, especially at its sunlit edges.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same droplets; grey means too thick for light

explain.say: A thick storm cloud can be over 10 kilometres deep. Light gets scattered and bounced around so much that most of it is sent back up or out of the sides, and little reaches the bottom.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same droplets; grey means too thick for light

explain.say: So the cloud's base looks dark grey, not because it is dirty, but because it is in its own shadow. A dark base often means the cloud holds lots of water, and rain may be coming.

draw.name: x-compare

faq.a: Cloud droplets are much bigger than air molecules, so they scatter all colours of sunlight about equally. All the colours mixed together look white.
asks: Why is a cloud not blue like the sky?

faq.a: Storm clouds are very thick and full of water and ice. Most sunlight is scattered back out of the top and sides, so very little reaches the base, which looks dark grey.
asks: Why do rain clouds look black?

faq.q: Does a grey cloud mean rain?
faq.a: Often. A dark base usually means the cloud is thick and loaded with water, which is what rain needs. But a cloud can also look grey just because another cloud is shading it.
asks: Will it rain if clouds are grey?

faq.q: Why are clouds pink at sunset?
faq.a: At sunset the light reaching the clouds has lost most of its blue on its long path through the air. White cloud droplets scatter whatever colour arrives, so they glow red, orange or pink.
asks: Why do clouds change colour at sunset?

faq.q: How much does a cloud weigh?
faq.a: A typical fluffy cumulus cloud holds hundreds of tonnes of water, spread out as tiny droplets through a huge volume of air. A big thunderstorm can hold millions of tonnes.

facts: Cloud droplets, about 0.02 millimetres across, are tens of thousands of times wider than air molecules.
A big thunderstorm cloud can tower more than 10 kilometres high.
